grammar.title: です/ます form (polite present)
grammar.explanation: Japanese uses です after nouns/adjectives and ます after verb stems for polite, neutral speech - the standard beginner register.
grammar.example: 私は学生です。毎日勉強します。

grammar.title: います/あります and Numbers 1-20
grammar.explanation: Use います for people/animals and あります for objects to say 'there is/are'. Numbers 1-20: いち、に、さん...にじゅう.
grammar.example: 兄が一人います。本が二十冊あります。

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.line: 兄弟がいますか。
dialogue.translation: Do you have siblings?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: はい、兄と姉が一人ずついます。
dialogue.translation: Yes, I have one older brother and one older sister.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.line: お仕事は何ですか。
dialogue.translation: What do they do for work?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: 兄はエンジニアで、姉は先生です。
dialogue.translation: My brother is an engineer, my sister is a teacher.

weeks.cultureNote: Japanese distinguishes older/younger siblings (兄/弟, 姉/妹) with different words - there's no single word for 'brother' or 'sister'. 週の終わりにレベル別スピーキング面接を行います。

grammarDeepDive.explanation: Passive voice: verb stem + られます/れます, used in formal/written Japanese to focus on the action or affected party.

Speaking and writing in this app follow JF Standard Can-do practice and are not part of the official JLPT.
